answer.rationale: The 18% cut is the dominant constraint; memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit-cost savings with reliable invoicing, and memory_c4 shows negotiation can extract further margin. However, delivery risk is acute (94% capacity, no buffer, 14-day expiry), so I verify memory_c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor's track record is as solid as summarized before committing. If the archived record confirms quick onboarding and accurate delivery, switching primary supply addresses the cost mandate directly without adding complexity. memory_c4 is verified secondarily to gauge whether a simultaneous quick negotiation with the incumbent on price/terms is viable as a fallback if the switch reveals risk in the archived detail. I am not proceeding to add_second_source or multi-year lock (memory_c3, memory_c6) this cycle because capacity is limited to one decision and the immediate contract gap must be closed first. Uncertainty acknowledged: the archived source for memory_c2 may reveal onboarding caveats (lead-time, qualification steps) that would make a 14-day window too tight, in which case renew_incumbent paired with negotiate_terms becomes the safer play.
